decisions.reason: The original per-member quantifier permitted arbitrary hard-coded, noncomputable sequences. One fixed index-to-description algorithm now witnesses uniformity. The fixed entry evaluator, exact-matrix promises, and per-instance encoding interface are preserved. Direct consumers use the entry evaluator rather than per-member advice.

Polynomial bounds alone did not make the witness/workspace split computable: even a fixed total width can conceal an uncomputable split. The fixed unary-length generator now emits both widths and the complete circuit/output specification; one fixed algorithm evaluates acceptance. Workspace is explicitly initialized to zero without imposing the stronger exact clean-return contract. The isometry J_x and acceptance effect are unchanged.

For ordered pair (g_{d-1},y) with target bits (1,0), the native gate acts in reversed order, so the original construction implemented XVX instead of V. The final native block is now XVX precisely in that branch. Gray-path conjugation, determinant one, conditioned Cauchy evaluation, error budgets, and exact workspace uncomputation then remain valid. Statement unchanged.

L(n) counts records rather than bits. The proof now computes all B(n)=L(n)r(n) bits, with three type bits and two logarithmic-width address fields. This supplies every comparison in step 2.1 with its complete program record. Polynomial enumeration, exact reversible Boolean computation, fixed-arity controlled templates, and telescoping operator error are preserved; Statement unchanged.

The verifier interface is used explicitly in the inputs but omitted from direct deps, although already supplied transitively by the promise-class definition. Added its direct edge and clarified that each verifier receives zero-initialized workspace. Input copying uses only a classical basis string; blocks, workspaces, and measured tuples are disjoint, and exact rational rounding implements the midpoint threshold.

The clock summands are mutually orthogonal, so the displayed history has squared norm N^{-1} sum_t ||U_t...U_1 phi||^2=||phi||^2. The formula is retained for every vector, and the word normalized is now restricted exactly to unit initial vectors. This preserves the linear history map needed by kernel and compression arguments. Local windows, weights, and tensor ordering are unchanged.

The computation-first convention makes the conjugation identity I_comp tensor L_T, as direct multiplication of V_t^* U_t V_{t-1} verifies. Corrected the swapped factors and clarified history normalization. The cosine eigenvectors, endpoint equations, first nonzero eigenvalue, and sine chord bound establish the same kernel and gap; Statement unchanged.

The projection estimate holds for every qualifying integer but polynomial resources require an explicit bounded choice. The proof now chooses floor(2K+4K^2/g)+1 and bounds its magnitude and encoding length. Counting inverted clock pairs proves the legal kernel and unit illegal-clock gap; the strict penalty inequality then gives error below g/4. Statement unchanged.

The current published Chernoff supplier explicitly proves the single-Bernoulli centered exponential bound in proof step 6.1, including p=0,1 and every real parameter; step 7.1 proves each one-sided additive tail. F3 accurately says its proof establishes that estimate. Tensor-product eigenbases bound the operator generating function for arbitrary entangled witnesses, and t=2 gamma yields exp(-r gamma^2/2). No repair is warranted.

The current measurement-synthesis supplier proves the rounded Newton square-root Cauchy construction in proof step 2.2, explicitly treating eigenvalue zero, inverse conditioning, dyadic rounding, and polynomial bit cost. Applying that scalar case to the rational t_x and 1-t_x supplies exactly the normalization coin entries cited in step 2.1. The mixture and single-interpreter budgets leave length-only thresholds separated by g_*/4. No repair is warranted.

At t-2,t-1,t,t+1,t+2 the gates are exactly Z_f,Z_s,CZ,Z_f,Z_s, so their product is CZ: no H or other gate intervenes. The four-sector calculation gives a=(2,1/2,1/2,1), d=(-2,-1/2,-1/2,1); its endpoint matrices are compressed representatives, scoped by On S_prop1, not principal blocks before compression. All weights are positive path penalties with the stated common kernel. No edit is needed.

The endpoint identities are valid for arbitrary T>=1, but the original unconditional restatement of the padded KKR supplier obscured that generality. Defined S_prop directly by the linear full-history map, made the KKR identification conditional, and proved R*R=I and both endpoint compressions directly. This preserves the universal claim, including empty A, and yields the stated input gap and rejection-energy bounds without importing padding assumptions.

The cited approximate interpreter did not justify exact predicate compilation. Replaced that use by the Boolean-circuit supplier and an explicit exact compute/copy/uncompute construction with the synthesis lemma’s exact Toffoli word; therefore the original 3/4 and 1/4 bounds hold with zero compilation error. Also corrected padding to L-1 one-qubit steps while keeping the four Z steps adjacent to CZ. Four errors below 1/64 give NO>11/16 and YES<=1/4 before rationalization.

downstream_evidence.affected_use: Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, $0\le s(n)<c(n)\le1$ efficiently encoded rational thresholds, and $w(n),a(n)$ polynomially bounded witness and clean-ancilla lengths. Require $c(n)-s(n)\ge1/p(n)$ for some polynomially bounded positive $p$. Then $\Pi\in\mathrm{QMA}(c,s)$ if there is a full-list uniform verifier interface as in [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]] such that every $x\in Y$ has a witness density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c(|x|)$, and every $x\in N$ and every witness density operator satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\le s(|x|)$. Behavior outside $Y\cup N$ is unrestricted. The standard bounded-error class uses $c=2/3$ and $s=1/3$. The effect and probability are well-defined by [[lem-qa-33-witness-acceptance-effect]].
downstream_evidence.reason: The Definition explicitly requires the revised verifier interface, so computable widths are inherited. Each verifier has input register $X_n$, witness register $W_n$, zero-initialized workspace $A_n$, terminally measured tuple $O_n$, and total predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$. The admissible parameters are those of the verifier's promise-class contract, with $r$ polynomially bounded when polynomial resources are claimed.
